text:
bob_acme: hey team — rerank endpoint started throwing errors for us this morning. 502s and sometimes 500s when the candidate list contains complex emoji sequences or when we include some binary-ish bytes. noticed it with 👩‍⚕️ and when a pipeline accidentally injected '\\u0000' into the text. request id r-6a3f, timeframe ~2025-12-04T09:12:10Z
jen_support: thanks - can you paste a minimal reproducible payload (curl or python)? also which model and rerank config?
tariq_engineer: @jen_support i'll take a look once we have the payload. curious if it's the tokenizer choking or our transport layer. any raw bytes or escaped sequences? :eyes:
bob_acme: here is a sanitized curl that reproduces it for us. fails ~100% for us with that payload.
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXX' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{
    "input": "patient notes: Fever, cough, 👩‍⚕️\\u200d🩺 zero-width joiner test",
    "candidates": ["Normal vitals", "Needs evaluation\\u0000", "Follow-up recommended"]
  }'
```
jen_support: submitted to infra with the trace id above. @maya_sre can you pull the logs for r-6a3f?
maya_sre: got it, pulling. preliminary log shows the reranker process crashed with an assertion in string_utils when processing candidate[1] (contains '\\u0000'). stack: model-serving.cpp:343 -> tokenizer_bridge.cpp:58 -> rerank_handler.cpp:204. attaching snippet: 
```
[2025-12-04T09:12:11Z] ERROR rerank-handler request=r-6a3f pid=4521 msg="invalid encoding: unexpected null byte"
[2025-12-04T09:12:11Z] FATAL model-serving pid=4521 signal=SIGABRT at model-serving.cpp:343
```
tariq_engineer: interesting — assertion on null byte inside what we thought was a UTF-8 sanitized buffer. could be leftover bytes from our upstream transport (node lib) that doesn't strip embedded NULs. also the emoji sequence with ZWJ might be producing unexpected byte sequences depending on client encoding.
bob_acme: fwiw we send UTF-8 from node. the issue started after we added a 3rd-party sanitizer that sometimes replaces diacritics and accidentally leaves nulls. but the emoji case repros even without nulls for us (the ZWJ sequence alone sometimes causes a 502).
jen_support: ok let's gather repro variations: 1) candidates with explicit '\\u0000' 2) candidates with ZWJ emoji sequences (👩‍⚕️, 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦) 3) latin1 bytes mixed with emoji. can someone try the model locally? @tariq_engineer can you spin a local rerank with debug logging for the tokenizer and kernel selection?
tariq_engineer: copying a quick debug curl that logs tokenizer bytes on the server side. flipping on verbose tracing for the canary.
```
# server side debug toggle (internal)
echo "enable:rerank.tokenizer.trace=1" | curl -X POST --data-binary @- http://infra-admin.local/feature-toggle
```
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for release v2.14.3-canary by tariq_engineer — targets: rerank service (3 instances).
maya_sre: canary up, attaching trace id r-6a3f-1 for the reproduced request. dump shows the tokenizer receives bytes: 0x70 0x61 0x74 0x69 0x65 0x6e 0x74 0x20 0x6e 0x6f 0x74 0x65 0x73 0x3a 0x20 0x46 0x65 0x76 0x65 0x72 0x2c 0x20 0x63 0x6f 0x75 0x67 0x68 0x2c 0x20 0xF0 0x9F 0x91 0xA9 0xE2 0x80 0x8D 0xE2 0x9A 0x95 0x20 0x7A 0x77 0x6A 0x20 0x74 0x65 0x73 0x74 0x00 0x00 0x20 0x4E 0x65 0x65 0x64 0x73 0x20 0x65 0x76 0x61 0x6C 0x75 0x61 0x74 0x69 0x6F 0x6E

# note the two 0x00 bytes after 'test'

tariq_engineer: aha — we see NUL bytes inserted between codepoints. tokenizer code path uses std::string and later calls c_str() for some legacy C ext, which breaks when NULs appear. also the emoji ZWJ sequence bytes are valid UTF-8 but one rare sequence interacts with our normalization code and produces an out-of-range codepoint index in the fused tokenizer, triggering an exception we were swallowing and turning into 502.
jen_support: next steps? mitigation for customer?
maya_sre: short term: reject inputs with embedded NULs at ingress (400) and add a helpful error message. long term: sanitize/escape NULs (e.g., base64 candidate bodies) or handle length-based tokenization without c_str reliance. I'll open a mitigation PR and apply a rate-limited deploy to prod if tests pass.
tariq_engineer: i'll prepare a patch to tokenizer_bridge to avoid c_str calls and to validate codepoint boundaries before normalization. will add regression tests for ZWJ sequences and surrogate pairs.
bob_acme: appreciate quick turnaround. also we got billed for ~12 failed rerank calls while we were debugging — can that be credited? they were failing, not completed.
iris_billing: @bob_acme we will issue a credit for failed requests between 2025-12-04T09:10:00Z and 2025-12-04T09:20:00Z. please confirm the account id and I'll trigger the refund. no need to escalate to sales. :white_check_mark:
jen_support: tracking assignees: tariq_engineer (fix), maya_sre (mitigation + apply), jen_support (customer comms + confirm credit). will follow up in this thread with PR links and changelog.
tariq_engineer: created PR #4621 with tokenizer fix, unit tests for ZWJ/emoji sequences, and a sanitizer fallback. patch summary: avoid c_str, validate UTF-8 codepoint boundaries, replace embedded NULs with U+FFFD or reject depending on config.
jen_support: applied ingress validation rule in canary and tested with bob_acme's payload — canary returns 400 with message "embedded null bytes not allowed; please sanitize or use base64 encoding for binary content".
bob_acme: confirmed 400 behavior now — clearer error is great, and the credit info is fine. we'll patch our sanitizer and keep an eye on weird ZWJ cases. thanks everyone. :pray:
jen_support: closing loop: once PR #4621 merges and we roll to prod we will notify and coordinate an outbound changelog + migration note for customers that historically sent binary content in text fields.
deploy-bot: Release v2.14.3-canary -> v2.14.3 (promoted) by maya_sre after successful canary.
jen_support: marking this thread resolved for support. reopen if bob_acme sees regressions.
